title: Unramified and tame extensions under arbitrary local DVR base extension
statement: Let $R\hookrightarrow S$ be an injective local homomorphism of discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction fields $F\subseteq E$ and common residue characteristic $p>0$, where $p$ is prime. Let $T/F$ be a finite separable field extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Put $C=\operatorname{IntCl}_T(R)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. For each maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $C$, write $e_{\mathfrak n}$ for the positive integer satisfying $\mathfrak m_R C_{\mathfrak n}=\mathfrak m_{C_{\mathfrak n}}^{e_{\mathfrak n}}$, and write $k_{\mathfrak n}=C/\mathfrak n$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The algebra $T\otimes_F E$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] is a finite product of fields $\prod_i U_i$. Write $D_i=\operatorname{IntCl}_{U_i}(S)$. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $D_i$, the ring $(D_i)_{\mathfrak q}$ is a DVR, the inclusion $S\hookrightarrow(D_i)_{\mathfrak q}$ is local, and its residue extension is finite. If all $e_{\mathfrak n}=1$ and all $k_{\mathfrak n}/(R/\mathfrak m_R)$ are separable, then for every $i,\mathfrak q$ one has $\mathfrak m_S(D_i)_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak m_{(D_i)_{\mathfrak q}}$ and $(D_i/\mathfrak q)/(S/\mathfrak m_S)$ is separable. If instead all $e_{\mathfrak n}$ are prime to $p$ and the same residue extensions are separable, then every new ramification index, defined by $\mathfrak m_S(D_i)_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak m_{(D_i)_{\mathfrak q}}^{e_{i,\mathfrak q}}$, is prime to $p$ and every new residue extension is separable. Local means that the inverse image of the maximal ideal is the maximal ideal. No finiteness, completeness, or separability assumption on $S/R$ is made.

source.place: Tag 0EXY, lemma-tame-goes-up, assertions (1) and (2), with the finite separable normalization facts in Tag 09E8, remark-finite-separable-extension; definitions of tame and unramified immediately before Tag 0EXR.

proof.text: First, for any field extension $E/F$, a finite separable $T/F$ is etale, and remains etale over $E$ by base change. Apply the etale-algebra-over-a-field theorem to obtain $T\otimes_FE=\prod_iU_i$, with each $U_i/E$ finite separable. The base-change citation applies to the singleton cover $\operatorname{Spec}T\to\operatorname{Spec}F$, which is surjective because its rings are nonzero fields. We will use this same conclusion for other finite separable field extensions below.

Apply the finite case (a) of the algebraic-normalization structure theorem with the identity DVR map $S\to S$ and the field extension $U_i/E$. It gives the DVR localizations $(D_i)_{\mathfrak q}$ and finite residue extensions over $S/\mathfrak m_S$. Their structural maps from $S$ are injective and local: maximal ideals contract to $\mathfrak m_S$, and denominators outside the contracted prime are units. Their fraction fields are $U_i$. Explicitly, for $x\in U_i$ choose a monic equation over $E$ and a power $s$ of a uniformizer of $S$ making all coefficients of the equation for $sx$ integral; then $sx\in D_i$, so $x\in\operatorname{Frac}(D_i)$. The same observations apply to $C_{\mathfrak n}$ over $R$. This proves all unconditional clauses.

Suppose the original indices are one and the original residue extensions are separable. Fix $V=(D_i)_{\mathfrak q}$. The map $T\to U_i$ sends $C$ into $D_i$: a monic equation over $R$ is a monic equation over $S$. Contract $\mathfrak m_V$ to $\mathfrak n\subset C$. This prime contains a nonzero uniformizer of $R$, so it is maximal by the dimension-one assertion of the normalization structure theorem. Localization gives a local injection $C_{\mathfrak n}\to V$. The finite-separable-fraction theorem makes $C_{\mathfrak n}$ essentially of finite type over $R$. Its index-one equality and separable residue extension therefore give $\Omega_{C_{\mathfrak n}/R}=0$ by the local unramified criterion.

source.place: Tag 0EXY, case (1), expressed using the local criterion instead of a global etale model

proof.text: Apply the unramified compositum theorem with its $(R,V,A,T)$ equal to $(R,C_{\mathfrak n},S,(D_i)_{\mathfrak q})$ and its field equal to $U_i$. The maps and locality were checked above. Its algebra-generation hypothesis holds: the field factor $U_i$ is generated by the images of $E$ and $T$, since each pure tensor maps to the product of these images. Moreover $E=S[1/\pi]$ for a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$: writing its nonzero image as a unit times a positive power of an $S$-uniformizer proves this equality. Since $T$ contains $1/\pi$, the $S$-algebra generated by $T$ already contains $E$. The theorem gives essential finite type and zero differentials for $S\to(D_i)_{\mathfrak q}$. The local criterion gives precisely the required maximal-ideal equality and separable residue extension. Thus the whole unramified assertion is proved for arbitrary local DVR base extension; it may now be applied to other DVR pairs.

Now suppose the original extension is tame. Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$. Uniformizer-root domination supplies $m\geq1$ prime to $p$, a finite separable $T'/F$ containing $T$ and $F_m=F(a)$ with $a^m=\pi$, such that $T'/F_m$ is unramified over the DVR $R_m=R[a]$. Its residue field is $R/\mathfrak m_R$. This is an auxiliary extension, not a replacement of the field factors whose conclusion we must prove.

Fix a factor $U=U_i$ and a maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $D=\operatorname{IntCl}_U(S)$. The algebra $T'\otimes_TU$ is nonzero (tensor a $T$-basis of $T'$), finite etale over $U$, and hence has a field factor $W$. It contains $U$ and $T'$ compatibly over $T$ and is generated by them. Let $J=\operatorname{IntCl}_W(S)$. The inclusion $D\subseteq J$ is integral, since each element of $J$ already satisfies a monic equation over $S\subseteq D$. Lying over gives a prime $\mathfrak r$ of $J$ above $\mathfrak q$; it is maximal and $J_{\mathfrak r}$ is a DVR by the normalization structure theorem, since $W/E$ is finite separable. Write $Z=J_{\mathfrak r}$. Then $D_{\mathfrak q}\to Z$ is an injective local map.

source.place: Tag 0EXY, first omitted detail: lift each chosen branch before descending

proof.text: Inside $W$ put $L=E(a)$ and $B=\operatorname{IntCl}_L(S)$; contract $\mathfrak m_Z$ to $\mathfrak b\subset B$. Then $B_{\mathfrak b}$ is a DVR with fraction field $L$ and the induced map $R_m\to B_{\mathfrak b}$ is local: $a^m=\pi$ lies in its maximal ideal, so $a$ does too. It is injective as a map of subrings of $W$. The field $W$ is a factor of $T'\otimes_{F_m}L$: its image contains $U=E\cdot T$ and $T'$, hence generates $W$, and a finite-dimensional domain over $L$ is a field. Apply the already proved unramified assertion (steps 2–4) to $R_m\to B_{\mathfrak b}$ and $T'/F_m$. It follows that $Z/B_{\mathfrak b}$ has index one and separable residue extension. To identify the selected localization, use transitivity of integrality to identify normalization first over $S$ and then over $B$, and integral-closure localization to pass to $B_{\mathfrak b}$; contraction of $\mathfrak r$ then gives exactly $Z$.

source.place: Tag 0EXY, case (2), unramified extension over the selected root-field branch

proof.text: It remains to bound the index and residue extension of $L/E$. Write $\pi=u\theta^t$ in $S$, where $\theta$ is a uniformizer, $u$ a unit, and $t\geq1$. Put $g=\gcd(m,t)$, $h=m/g$, $d=t/g$. Choose $y$ with $y^h=\theta$ in an algebraic extension of $L$, put $V=L(y)$, and set $z=a/y^d$. Then $z^m=u$ and $a=zy^d$, so $V=E(y,z)$. By the uniformizer-root-algebra theorem $S_y=S[y]$ is a DVR with uniformizer $y$, fraction field $E(y)$, and residue field $S/\mathfrak m_S$ (reduce its presentation modulo $y$). The unit-binomial theorem says $S_y[Z]/(Z^m-u)$ is finite etale. Its generic field factor selected by $Z\mapsto z$ is precisely $V$. The normal-generic-components theorem identifies the corresponding component with $H=\operatorname{IntCl}_V(S_y)$ and makes it finite etale over $S_y$.

source.place: Tag 0EXY, last paragraph: explicit binomial chart and its normalization

proof.text: The ring $H$ is also the integral closure of $S$ in $V$: $S_y/S$ is integral, so transitivity gives one inclusion, while a monic equation over $S$ is also one over $S_y$. By lying over choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak h$ of $H$ above $\mathfrak b$ of $B$; here $H/B$ is integral because its elements are integral over $S$. Put $Q=H_{\mathfrak h}$. It is a DVR by the normalization structure theorem. Since $H/S_y$ is etale, the etale maximal-ideal and residue-field theorems give $\mathfrak m_{S_y}Q=\mathfrak m_Q$ and a finite separable residue extension. Consequently $y$ is a uniformizer of $Q$, and $\theta=y^h$ has valuation $h$ in $Q$.

source.place: Tag 0EXY, last omitted detail: choose a chart branch above the specified branch

proof.text: Let $b=e(B_{\mathfrak b}/S)$ and $c=e(Q/B_{\mathfrak b})$, both positive. If $\beta$ is a uniformizer of $B_{\mathfrak b}$, write $\theta=v\beta^b$ there with $v$ a unit; then in $Q$ it gives $h=bc$. Thus $b\mid h\mid m$, so $p\nmid b$. The local injection $B_{\mathfrak b}\to Q$ embeds its residue field into that of $Q$. Every element of this subfield is separable over $S/\mathfrak m_S$, since its minimal polynomial divides a separable polynomial for the same element in the larger field. Hence $B_{\mathfrak b}/S$ has separable residue extension. Together with step 7, the valuation formula in a DVR gives $e(Z/S)=b\cdot1=b$, and transitivity of separable algebraic extensions gives separability of $\kappa(Z)/\kappa(S)$.

source.place: Tag 0EXY, end of proof; explicit index and residue computations

proof.text: Finally apply the same valuation calculation to the tower $S\to D_{\mathfrak q}\to Z$. The positive index $e(D_{\mathfrak q}/S)$ divides $e(Z/S)$ and is therefore prime to $p$. The residue field $D/\mathfrak q$ embeds into $\kappa(Z)$, so its elements are separable over $S/\mathfrak m_S$ by the minimal-polynomial argument of step 10. Its degree is finite by step 2. The original factor $U_i$ and the prime $\mathfrak q$ were arbitrary; this gives every required tame branch, including the case $m=1$. No hypothesis on the degree, completeness or separability of $S/R$ was used.
